title: No format is leak-proof
statement: No item format is leak-proof and each leaks its own way, so test every item with the text hidden using a strong solver.
example: Under the first gate, 97% of multiple-choice items were answered without the passage, against 0% of matching items.
detail: A cross-family anti-leak gate recorded blind recovery by format: multiple-choice 97%, multiple-select 100% and two-part evidence items 80% were rejected, against hot-text 24%, sequence 42% and match 0%, which left a 541-slot skeleton only 32.7% fillable. After a passage-design fix the measured leak was 99.5% for multiple-choice, 100% for multiple-select and ~0.56% for the other formats. A strong-solver re-gate then left only 20 of 95 'clean' items and 187 of 3,146 untested candidates (5.9%), so the low rates depended on the solver. Single-choice items leak through general knowledge or a textbook-correct option, multi-select items through options that reinforce each other, highlight items through stems that signpost the span, and ordering items through events with a natural order. Design each format against its own leak, and prefer forms built to need the reading.
against: The project's plan notes hold that selected response is not inherently leaky, but raw selected-response items often are, and that hot-text and sequence formats need extra suspicion because renderer, protocol and guessability issues can masquerade as content quality (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0090-fable5-plan-traces-2026-07-09.qmd`, lines 132 and 134). The fix list's audits were all same-family, so its closed leaks have no cross-family solve behind them (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0236-g5-package-build-facts-and-g3-fixlist-apply-2026-07-02.qmd`). The Grade 5 figures are historical, kept as pricing and design evidence, not current readiness (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/practice-layer-spec.md`, line 20). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g5-reading/assessments/DESIGN.md`).
